what_its_for: Aripiprazole lauroxil is used to treat schizophrenia in adults. Schizophrenia is a mental health condition that can cause symptoms like hearing or seeing things that are not there (hallucinations), believing things that are not true (delusions), and disorganized thinking. This medicine helps reduce these symptoms and helps you think more clearly and feel more stable.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a shot (injection) by a doctor, nurse, or other healthcare provider. It is NOT something you give yourself at home. The shot is usually given in the upper arm (deltoid muscle) or the buttocks (gluteal muscle). You will need to visit your healthcare provider regularly to get your injections on schedule. Do not skip appointments, even if you are feeling well.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you. Common doses range from 441 mg to 1064 mg given once a month, every 6 weeks, or every 2 months depending on which strength your doctor prescribes. When you first start this medicine, you may also receive an injection of Aristada Initio (a single starting shot) along with oral aripiprazole tablets for 21 days, OR you may need to take aripiprazole pills by mouth for 21 days to build up enough medicine in your body. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for getting started.
missed_dose: If you miss a scheduled injection appointment, contact your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not wait until your next regular appointment. Depending on how long it has been since your last shot, your doctor may need to adjust your treatment plan or restart you on oral medication temporarily. Missing doses can cause your symptoms to come back, so staying on schedule is very important.
storage: This medicine is stored and handled by your healthcare provider or pharmacy. You do not need to store it at home. If you are given any oral aripiprazole tablets to take at home, store them at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep all medications away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight, and out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while using this medicine, as it can increase dizziness, drowsiness, and other side effects. Be careful when driving, operating heavy machinery, or doing anything that requires you to be alert, especially when you first start treatment, because this medicine may cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid getting overheated or becoming dehydrated, especially in hot weather or during exercise, as this medicine can affect your body's ability to regulate temperature. Tell your doctor before taking any new prescription or over-the-counter medicines, vitamins, or herbal supplements, as some medications can interact with aripiprazole.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the nearest emergency room if you experience any of the following: thoughts of harming yourself or others, new or worsening depression or anxiety, uncontrollable movements of your face, tongue, or body (may be a sign of a serious condition called tardive dyskinesia), stiffness, high fever, confusion, or fast heartbeat (signs of neuroleptic malignant syndrome, a rare but serious reaction), trouble swallowing, seizures, significant weight gain, changes in blood sugar (increased thirst, frequent urination, blurry vision), fainting or feeling very lightheaded when standing up, or signs of low white blood cell count such as fever, chills, or frequent infections.
when_it_works: Aripiprazole lauroxil starts releasing medication into your body slowly after the injection. Some people begin to notice improvement in their symptoms within the first few weeks, but it may take several weeks to a few months to feel the full benefit of the medicine. It is important to keep all your injection appointments and not stop treatment just because you are feeling better. Stopping suddenly can cause your symptoms to return.
special_populations: Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis should NOT use this medicine, as antipsychotic medicines like aripiprazole lauroxil can increase the risk of death in this group. This medicine is not approved for use in children or teenagers. If you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, talk to your doctor right away. Babies born to mothers who took antipsychotic medicine during the third trimester of pregnancy may have temporary withdrawal symptoms or muscle problems after birth. It is not fully known if aripiprazole passes into breast milk, so talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. If you have diabetes, liver problems, heart problems, low blood pressure, a history of seizures, or trouble swallowing, make sure your doctor knows before starting this medicine.
